reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern consists of a quasi-periodic sequence of sharp, narrow upward spikes (duration ~5–10 points) followed by rapid decay to near-zero baseline, recurring approximately every 98 points (consistent with estimated period). Each spike reaches robust-standardized values between ~12 and ~19, with 90th-percentile amplitude ~17–19 across candidates. Baseline is stable near zero (median 0.0–0.16), with low roughness (~0.166) and mild curvature (~0.168–0.171), indicating smooth low-frequency drift rather than noise. Slope per point is near-zero (±0.009), confirming absence of strong trend. Peaks are asymmetric: steep rise (~2–3 points), slower fall (~5–8 points); troughs are flat and shallow (near 0), occasionally dipping slightly negative. Noise in baseline segments is low-amplitude (<1) and irregular but non-oscillatory. Acceptable variation includes minor differences in spike height (±1–2 units), exact timing jitter (±2–3 points), and baseline offset (≤0.2), but not sustained elevation, broad plateaus, or extra/missing spikes within a cycle. Boundary truncation is minimal; all candidates show full cycles at interior segments.
